gaps.lead: I only understood the pattern much later.
gaps.explanation: Front 'only + time phrase' forces inversion: Only much later did I understand.

gaps.lead: I have never read such a gripping novel.
gaps.sentence: This is ___ I have ever read.
gaps.explanation: 'Never read such a gripping novel' = 'the most gripping novel I have ever read'.

gaps.lead: 'I'm sorry I was so rude to your sister,' Maria said.
gaps.sentence: Maria apologised ___ so rude to my sister.
gaps.explanation: apologise for + -ing: apologised for being so rude.

gaps.lead: His trainers were so worn out that they had holes in them.
gaps.sentence: His trainers were ___ they had holes in them.
gaps.explanation: so worn out = in such bad condition.

gaps.lead: 'Have you seen my keys anywhere?' he asked us.
gaps.sentence: He asked us ___ his keys anywhere.
gaps.explanation: if/whether + subject + backshifted verb: whether we had seen.

gaps.lead: The company has a good reputation in the local area.
gaps.sentence: The company ___ of in the local area.
gaps.explanation: 'People speak highly of it' becomes the passive 'it is highly spoken of'.
